methodology_and_limitations: Every one of the 34 frozen evidence_scope entries in the golden opportunity manifest pins a single-point anchor (start_line == end_line in all 34 cases); none independently pins a second, distinct line for a correlated signal (e.g. a separate judge-configuration line for an EVL-002 opportunity whose anchor is the producer call). Whole-file source bytes for the golden cohort are not committed to this repository -- per protocol.md section 5 step 8, the source-evidence index retains only digests in public/internal artifacts inspected here, and no external repository source was fetched to fill that gap (fetching live external source was treated as out of scope for this action item and was not attempted).

Per discovery-anchor-contract-v1.9.json, each rule's candidate_normalization groups multiple contributing signals (producer, alias, helper, sink, judge, rubric, etc.) into one candidate anchored at a single canonical_locus line. That the methodology normalizes to one anchor does not by itself prove every contributing signal is textually co-located in the same file as the anchor -- the normalization is about where the finding is reported, not about the span of code that was read to support it. This document therefore treats a single-point anchor as inconclusive on its own, and only classifies an opportunity file-local when an independent, frozen corroborating signal is also present (see evidence_categories_used below). Where no such corroboration exists, the item is recorded ambiguous/cross-module rather than assumed file-local by default.

Corroborating signals used, all drawn from committed v1.9 artifacts: (a) same-repository/same-rule opportunities that all anchor to one file, especially when their lines are textually adjacent (a strong same-block signal); (b) golden execution-evidence coverage counts (sourceFilesConsidered / sourceFilesWithLlmIndicators) that bound how many files in a repository could plausibly carry a second correlated signal; (c) the discovery-anchor-contract's own canonical_locus/candidate_normalization text for the applicable rule; (d) golden-manifest repository metadata (primary_surface, inclusion_reason) that names an architecture pattern (e.g. a declared graph/node evaluation framework, or a monorepo with separate app/package directories) independent of any specific line of code.

None of these corroborating signals amounts to reading the actual defect's source code; every file-local classification below is therefore an inference from committed metadata and layout, not a confirmed reading of co-located evidence, and is worded accordingly. Cross-module classifications with strong corroboration (M3/M4/M5 below) are similarly inferences from layout and naming convention, not confirmed readings. Only 9 of the 34 rows have no corroborating signal at all in the frozen artifacts; those are recorded ambiguous with owner_review_flag=true rather than guessed in either direction.

One golden repository's execution receipt (Ankitha-GS/rag-qa) additionally records that the origin no longer resolves on GitHub as of the most recent re-execution -- independent confirmation that live external re-inspection of golden source is not an available or reproducible substitute for the missing committed whole-file evidence in this cycle, reinforcing why this document does not attempt to fetch external source.

This is a structural, engineering-scoping conclusion, not a performance or ground-truth-correctness conclusion: it estimates how many of the 34 misses look reachable by improving same-file pattern matching versus how many plausibly require new cross-file/interprocedural tracing capability, given what the frozen v1.9 artifacts show -- it is not a claim about what the underlying repository code definitely does, and it does not relabel any opportunity's present/absent ground truth.

classification_definitions.file_local: All decisive evidence needed to satisfy the opportunity's rule-specific required-evidence checklist is inferred, with at least one corroborating signal beyond the single-point anchor itself, to be observable within the single file named in evidence_scope.path_or_reference.
classification_definitions.cross_module: The rule's required-evidence checklist plausibly or demonstrably needs evidence correlated from a second, different file than evidence_scope.path_or_reference (a separate producer/judge/config/orchestrator module, a separate presentation-layer file, or a separate package in a monorepo), based on a corroborating signal in the frozen artifacts.
classification_definitions.ambiguous: Per the operating instruction for this action item, ambiguous is recorded as classification=cross-module with ambiguous=true and owner_review_flag=true, used whenever no corroborating signal (M1-M5 below) is available in any frozen artifact -- the single-point anchor alone is treated as insufficient to assert file-local, and asserting cross-module with confidence would equally overreach, so it is flagged for human (or a further independent) review rather than guessed.
classification_definitions.reconciliation_note: Superseded by review_and_reconciliation: two isolated AI review passes found every row (not only the 9 originally marked ambiguous) genuinely ambiguous under this document's own evidentiary standard, since none of the M1-M5 signals amount to affirmative architectural evidence. All 34 rows are therefore now recorded ambiguous=true, owner_review_flag=true, classification=cross-module (the mandated conservative fallback), with semantic_status of indeterminate (24 explicit-contract rows) or out_of_explicit_contract (10 non-enumerated-rule rows) tracked separately in review_and_reconciliation.

evidence_categories_used: M1 same-file clustering: 2+ opportunities for the same repository+rule anchor to one file, especially with textually adjacent lines -> supports file-local
